key_insight: Bi-FORK learns to model bifurcating physical systems where one input can lead to multiple valid outcomes, replacing the usual one-to-one prediction assumption with a generative one-to-many framework. It enables complete trajectory generation in high-dimensional settings where symmetry breaking creates branching solution paths.
problem_solved: Most learned physical surrogate models assume a unique output for each input, which breaks down at bifurcations. This paper addresses the challenge of predicting multiple equally valid solutions in complex high-dimensional systems.
method: Introduces Bi-FORK, a generative modeling framework for bifurcating systems.
Learns one-to-many solution maps instead of forcing a single deterministic prediction.
Generates complete trajectories that capture branching behavior after symmetry breaking.
impact: This is important for AI/ML practitioners building surrogate models for scientific computing, because many real-world systems are inherently multi-solution. Bi-FORK opens the door to more faithful, uncertainty-aware modeling of phenomena in mechanics, fluids, and climate science.
visual_elements: Branching trajectory diagram showing one input splitting into multiple valid outputs
Before-vs-after comparison of deterministic surrogate models vs generative bifurcation modeling
Symmetry-breaking illustration with a system transitioning from stable to split states
High-dimensional solution manifold or latent space visualization
paper_title: Bi-FORK: Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Bifurcating Systems
paper_authors: Anna Zimmel, Fleur Hendriks, Markus Holzleitner, Florian Sestak, Martin Weichselbaumer
